properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled; recorded as a minor idea with a real objection.

THE IDEA: percentile and median (unused, in dynograph-vector::stats) would let surprising_connections report "the top 5% most surprising couplings in THIS design" rather than everything over a fixed score. A distributional cut self-calibrates to the graph it is run on; an absolute one does not, and a design with 100 nodes and one with 10,000 do not have the same natural scale.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is the projects own lesson: BL-23 established that when a detector punishes correct work, the answer is A DIFFERENT QUESTION, not a tuned threshold. A percentile is still a threshold — it just moves rather than sits still. Worse, a top-N-percent rule ALWAYS returns something, so a design with no surprising couplings at all would still be handed a list, which is exactly the false-signal failure the noise-floor work (BL-42) was about.

WHERE IT MIGHT STILL HELP: not as a cut, but as CONTEXT on a finding already made — "surprise 2.56, which is the highest in this design" is more useful to a reader than a bare number, and asserts nothing extra.
properties.name: OPEN — should surprise and severity be reported as distributional positions rather than absolute scores?
properties.rationale: Kept deliberately small and recorded with the objection first, because the naive form of this idea contradicts an established lesson and a later session should meet the objection at the same moment as the idea.
